subject: Aligning pilot success metrics and access commitments
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@clearbridgehealth.com>, Laura Greene <laura@clearbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Aligning pilot success metrics and access commitments

Hi Samir & Laura,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the candid conversation about the two places ClearBridge wants immediate improvements: faster triage of provider notes and reducing false positives in the billing reconciliation workflow. Quick recap and proposed lightweight pilot so we can validate throughput, accuracy delta, and operational fit.

Key pain & goals (as discussed)
- Current manual triage for provider notes takes ~18-24 hours per case; target pilot goal is 6 hours or less where automation is used.
- Billing reconciliation false positives cost ~2 FTEs/week; target metric is 30% reduction in false positives for the pilot scope.
- Data sensitivity: PHI in notes, on-prem connectors preferred for the first phase.

Proposed pilot scope (30 days)
- Scope: ~10K anonymized notes (subset of ambulatory), plus 2 billing reconciliation flows (claims mismatch).
- Success metrics: end-to-end latency (median inference latency per request), accuracy (precision/recall on labeled sample), false-positive reduction percentage, infra stability (error rate < 1%).
- Owners: ClearBridge owners = Samir (PM), Laura (Data ENG); Redwood owners = Mina (Engg lead), Ben (CS/ops), Olga (Security).
- Deliverables: prompt & eval set, baseline model run, one iteration of prompt rework and rerun, final readout.

Access and setup items (actionable)
1) ClearBridge creates a service account for Redwood with read-only access to S3 bucket "cbh-pilot-data" and shares a short-term decryption key for encrypted extracts.
2) Network: allow outbound to redwood-dedicated.redwood.ai on ports 443/22 for private connector setup (we will request exact IP ranges in follow-up).
3) Data format: CSV with columns [note_id, text, label_flag]; sample schema will be attached.

Attachments: pilot-charter.xlsx (first draft of scope & timeline)

Ask: Can you confirm the owners above and the S3 service-account work? If yes, we will schedule a 60-minute kickoff (tech + security) next week and circulate a compact runbook for the private connector.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: pilot-charter.xlsx (12KB, xlsx)

From: Samir Patel <samir@clearbridgehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Greene <laura@clearbridgehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 16:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aligning pilot success metrics and access commitments

Mina — thanks for the clear recap. That matches what we took away. A couple quick clarifications: 

- Data sensitivity: we can provide a de-identified export initially, but we need to validate the private-connector flow against a sub-production environment before sending any PHI. Our security team will need the runbook you mentioned.
- Metrics: for the false-positive reduction target, can we also include a short definition doc so everyone is aligned on how ClearBridge labels a false positive? I can share a 2-page rubric.

Confirm owners: Samir (PM) and Laura (Data ENG) are confirmed — adding our security lead Tom Reyes (tom.reyes@clearbridgehealth.com) to advocate for the connector review.

We can do kickoff the morning of Dec 13th PST — does that work for the Redwood team?

Best,
Samir
Product Lead, ClearBridge Health

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@clearbridgehealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aligning pilot success metrics and access commitments

> Key pain & goals (as discussed)
> - Current manual triage for provider notes takes ~18-24 hours per case; target pilot goal is 6 hours or less where automation is used.

Quick confirm from my side: Redwood will allocate the following resources for the 30-day pilot — 1 GPU instance for baseline runs, a dedicated private connector engineer (Olga/Ben pairing), and weekly syncs. I will own the run cadence and coordinate the baseline vs. improved evals.

I will also drop the initial infra checklist into the shared drive later today (link to follow).

—Ben

Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@clearbridgehealth.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@clearbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Laura Greene <laura@clearbridgehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2027 09:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aligning pilot success metrics and access commitments

Thanks everyone — alignment looks good. Confirmed next steps and owners (action table):

- ClearBridge: create S3 service account + share sample (due: Dec 10) — owner: Samir.
- ClearBridge Security: review private connector runbook and confirm network/IP allowlist (due: Dec 11) — owner: Tom.
- Redwood: provide initial baseline evaluation and prompt set (due: Dec 15) — owner: Ben.
- Redwood: set up private connector in staging and validate transfer (due: Dec 12) — owner: Olga.
- Joint: Kickoff meeting (60m) — proposed Dec 13 09:30 PST; Ben will send calendar invite.

Attached I’ve uploaded the initial prompt set and a lightweight evaluation rubric for your review: prompt-set-v1.csv (5KB) and the rubric is at the HubSpot link below. Please flag any misalignments to the metrics definitions by EOD Dec 10 so we can freeze the eval sample.

If there are no blockers from security, we will begin ingesting the de-identified sample by Dec 12 and run the baseline within 48 hours.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
